title-lg.purpose: Editor page headers and onboarding dialog title.

title-sm.purpose: Panel headings such as the library title.

body.purpose: Default text, inputs, textareas, dialog copy.

label.purpose: Buttons, tool buttons, field labels, list names, node titles.

caption.purpose: Rail labels, badges, edge labels, list meta, hints. The 12px floor.

mono.purpose: Code editor, file paths, IDs, API provider marks.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting lift for buttons, workflow nodes, edge labels.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Node hover and selection; edge delete popover.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Floating layers: profile menu, toasts, dialogs, test panel, sliding inspector.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Focused fields and search box; selected node (combined with shadow-md).

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring on every interactive element.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Standard ease-out for all state transitions and overlays.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, press, border, color and focus transitions.

motion.name: t
motion.purpose: Overlay entrances (menu pop-in, toast rise, dialog rise and scale) and the sliding inspector.

motion.name: pulse-dot
motion.purpose: Running test and connection-checking status dots only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables animation and transition.

icons.system: Inline SVG sprite <symbol id="i-*"> (24px grid, 1.7 stroke) plus CSS mask icons --ico-* (1.9 stroke) for button leading icons; round caps and joins; currentColor.

narrative.overview:
Workflow Studio is a category-standard desktop workbench executed at the craft level of Linear, Figma and Lark. Every screen answers three questions and nothing more: where am I, what state is this in, what do I do next. The world is cool neutral and light by default, following the operating system into a full dark theme; structure comes from three stacked neutral surfaces separated by 1px hairlines, not from color or decoration.

Color is rationed by meaning. One blue accent marks the single next step, selection, focus and the current path. Resource type colors live only inside small type-icon tiles. Status colors appear only where a status is being stated. Everything else is gray, so that when color shows up it is information.

Density is professional but legible: a 14px body, a 12px floor, system UI faces in Chinese and Latin, tabular numerals for counts. Motion is short and functional (140 to 200ms ease-out) and exists only for state changes and floating layers. The interface rejects the category's default near-black node editor with neon nodes, purple AI glows, gradients, uppercase English kickers and tiny 6 to 9px text.
keyCharacteristics: Light-first, cool-neutral, system dark theme via `prefers-color-scheme` with every token remapped.
Three-surface layering (white content and canvas chrome, light-gray rail and library, dotted canvas) bounded by 1px hairlines.
One blue accent; type colors confined to 20 to 32px icon tiles; status colors confined to status carriers.
One shared status vocabulary (draft / ready / synced / conflict) with a three-dot lifecycle marker.
Exactly one filled primary button per context, representing the next step.
Narrow windows condense controls to icon buttons; nothing is removed.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent is reserved for the next step, selection, focus and the current path. It never decorates, never becomes a gradient and never glows.

rules.name: The Tile-Only Type Color Rule
rules.body: Agent, Action, Skill and Workflow colors live only inside their type-icon tiles. If a type color appears outside a tile, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Meaning-Bound Status Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only where they state a status or a danger. Settled states stay neutral.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text renders below .75rem (12px). There are no literal pixel font sizes; every size comes from the --fs-* ramp (12 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 18 / 20 / 24).

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Counts, IDs and paths use tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) or the mono stack so columns of numbers do not jitter.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No uppercase English labels above headings; nothing in the build uses `text-transform: uppercase`. Context such as the current project name sits below the heading as a plain 12px tertiary subtitle.

rules.name: The Nothing Disappears Rule
rules.body: At every width each action stays reachable; secondary actions shrink to icon buttons with accessible names rather than being hidden.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Weight Rule
rules.body: Only things that float above the workspace get the overlay shadow. Panels inside the grid never cast shadows; they are separated by hairlines.

dos: **Do** keep exactly one accent-filled primary button per context, and make it the next step (publish while draft, sync once published).
**Do** express every resource state with the shared badge vocabulary and lifecycle dots: draft, ready, synced, conflict.
**Do** separate destructive actions from their siblings with extra space and danger tint.
**Do** condense secondary actions to 32px icon buttons with accessible names below 1240px instead of hiding them.
**Do** use the 2px focus outline at 2px offset on every interactive element, and the 3px focus halo on fields.
**Do** keep motion to 140 to 200ms on `cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1)` for state changes and floating layers, and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** remap tokens for dark theme rather than writing per-component dark overrides.
donts: **Don't** set text below 12px or use literal pixel font sizes outside the --fs-* ramp.
**Don't** use type colors outside type-icon tiles, or status colors where no status is stated.
**Don't** badge settled synced rows in lists.
**Don't** use dark neon node-editor styling, purple AI glows, gradients or decorative glow shadows.
**Don't** add uppercase English kickers or eyebrows above headings.
**Don't** give in-grid panels drop shadows; reserve the overlay shadow for floating layers.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons; use the linear SVG set.
